name: Monitor market rule compliance and respond to the MSA
summary: Alberta generators must follow the AESO's ISO rules on offers, restatements, dispatch and outages and the Alberta reliability standards, and the Market Surveillance Administrator (MSA) enforces them. The market compliance officers review possible breaches found by daily checks, traders or the cyber team, decide whether a rule was broken, self-report contraventions with corrective actions to win forbearance, and answer MSA inquiries and AESO referrals with legal help. The work turns on judgment about the rule wording and offer reasons, a 30-day window for self-reports, and MSA decisions that take weeks to months.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with several pool participant entities and a small market compliance team in its regulatory department.
baseline.notes: TransAlta entities received 14 ISO rules and 1 O&P ARS notices of specified penalty in 2021 (MSA Compliance Review 2021); with about 10 percent of self-reports drawing a penalty, that implies on the order of 100 self-reported matters a year, plus internal reviews that find no contravention and MSA inquiries.

trigger: A possible contravention is flagged by the daily offer checks, a trader, operator or the cyber team, or the MSA or AESO sends an inquiry or referral.
end_state: The matter is closed internally with a documented no-contravention rationale, or closed after an MSA disposition with any penalty paid and corrective actions complete.

volume.seasonality: More restatement and dispatch matters in volatile months (winter peaks, summer heat) and during plant conversions and outage seasons.

surge.cause: Alberta reliability standards compliance audit, run on a three-year cycle, which brings evidence requests and self-reports

evidence.note: The MSA notes that O&P ARS matter counts vary with the three-year audit cycle; duration and multiplier are the author's estimates.
Derived from TransAlta's 15 penalty matters in 2021 and the 10 percent penalty rate on self-reports, plus internal reviews closed without a report; the organisation file range is kept.

systems.name: AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
Energy trading and risk management system
Document management and engineering drawings repository
ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)

steps.name: Log the potential issue or inquiry
steps.description: The market compliance officer logs the item in the compliance tracker: a possible contravention flagged by the daily offer and restatement exception report, a trader or operator, a reliability standard evidence gap from the cyber team, or a letter from the MSA or the AESO, and assigns an owner.
inputs: exception report, desk flag, CIP evidence or MSA letter

evidence.note: In 2021, 91 percent of ISO rules matters reaching the MSA were self-reported and 9 percent came from AESO referrals; the share of MSA-initiated cases here also covers information requests and is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Gather the facts
steps.description: The officer pulls the offer and restatement history and dispatch acknowledgements from the AESO Energy Trading System, the dispatch log, historian trends and desk logbooks or chat, and builds a timeline of what happened against the rule's deadlines.

next.condition: ISO rules matter (offers, restatements, dispatch, outages, operating reserves)

evidence.note: Most ISO rules matters concern restatements (203.3), delivery under dispatch (203.4, 205.5, 205.6) and dispatch acknowledgement (201.7); ISO rules matters outnumber company-relevant ARS matters. Times estimated.

steps.name: Desk lead explains the trading event
steps.description: The real-time desk lead reviews the timeline with the trader or control room operator involved, explains why an offer was restated late, a dispatch was missed or a unit under-delivered, and identifies what in the tools or procedures allowed it.

evidence.note: Desk leads work extended hours; availability wait estimated.

steps.name: Cyber or OT team explains the evidence gap
steps.description: A cyber security analyst explains why reliability standard evidence is missing or late, for example an access review, patch assessment or configuration baseline for a plant control system that was not done on schedule, and what was affected.

evidence.note: CIP-004, CIP-007 and CIP-010 were the most frequent CIP matters in 2021; the step is the author's description.

steps.name: Assess whether a rule was contravened
steps.description: The officer compares the facts with the exact wording of the ISO rule or reliability standard, its compliance exceptions and past MSA dispositions, and decides whether a contravention occurred and whether it is part of a recurring problem.

error.defect_description: A contravention is judged not to have occurred, or a recurring pattern is missed.

evidence.note: Share of internal reviews that find no contravention is the author's estimate; experience-heavy judgment as the organisation file notes.

steps.name: Record the no-contravention rationale and close
steps.description: The officer writes a short rationale citing the rule and the facts, attaches the evidence to the tracker so it can be shown to an auditor or the MSA later, and closes the item.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Agree corrective actions
steps.description: The officer agrees with the desk lead, plant or cyber team what will prevent a repeat, such as coaching, a new alarm in the offer tool or a changed procedure, and for reliability standard matters drafts a mitigation plan with dates.
outputs: corrective action plan or mitigation plan

evidence.note: Corrective actions support forbearance and mitigation plans are expected with reliability standard self-reports (sections 4.1, 5.3 and 6.4).

steps.name: Draft the self-report
steps.description: The officer completes the MSA self-report form with the rule section, timeline, impact on the market or system, root cause, mitigating circumstances and corrective actions, aiming to file within 30 days of the contravention to keep forbearance available.

error.defect_description: The form omits required information or the file date slips past 30 days.

control.basis: MSA Compliance Process sections 3.1, 4.1 and 5.3: self-report on the MSA form within 30 days to qualify for forbearance; duty to comply under Electric Utilities Act section 20.8

evidence.note: Form contents and forbearance criteria from the MSA Compliance Process; drafting time estimated.

steps.name: Legal review of a complex matter
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews self-reports and responses that could lead to an administrative penalty or an AUC proceeding, checks the wording of admissions and privilege, and advises on what to disclose.

evidence.note: Serious matters may go to the AUC under section 51 of the AUCA (section 7 of the Compliance Process); review share and times estimated.

steps.name: Director approves the submission
steps.description: The director of health, safety, environment and regulatory reads the self-report or inquiry response, confirms the facts and corrective actions with the business owner, and approves it for filing.

control.basis: Market compliance program: director sign-off on submissions to regulators

evidence.note: Sign-off practice estimated.

steps.name: File the submission with the MSA
steps.description: The officer emails the self-report or response to compliance@albertamsa.ca with a copy to the AESO compliance mailbox, or uses a secure channel for sensitive CIP information, and records the filing in the tracker.

control.basis: MSA Compliance Process sections 3.1 and 3.2: submissions to compliance@albertamsa.ca copying the AESO; sensitive CIP information by an agreed channel

steps.name: MSA assesses the matter
steps.description: The MSA acknowledges the filing with a file number, reviews the information and any AESO referral material, and either asks the company further questions or issues a disposition.

evidence.note: With 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 and 56 unresolved at year end, the average time a matter waits at the MSA is roughly 56/462 of a year, about 44 days; the spread and the follow-up share are estimates.

steps.name: Answer the MSA's follow-up questions
steps.description: The officer gathers the extra data or explanation the MSA requested, has the desk or cyber team check it, and sends a written answer, usually within two weeks.

control.basis: Alberta Utilities Commission Act: MSA information requests must be answered

evidence.note: The process says the MSA may request more information and allows submissions within two weeks of a referral; times estimated.

steps.name: Record the MSA's disposition
steps.description: The officer records the disposition (forbearance, conditional forbearance, no contravention or notice of specified penalty) in the tracker, tells the business owner and updates the count used for repeat-contravention escalation.

evidence.note: In 2021, 10 percent of self-reported and 77 percent of referred ISO rules matters drew a specified penalty; 12 percent is a blend for this case mix.

steps.name: Arrange payment of the specified penalty
steps.description: The officer confirms with the director that the company will pay rather than dispute, raises a payment request with accounts payable for the amount set under AUC Rule 019 or 027, and files proof of payment.

control.basis: Alberta Utilities Commission Act section 52 and AUC Rules 019 and 027: specified penalties paid or disputed before the AUC

evidence.note: No specified penalty was disputed or unpaid in 2021; payment handling estimated.

steps.name: Close corrective actions and update desk guidance
steps.description: The officer checks that the corrective actions or mitigation plan are complete, reports completion to the MSA within five business days where a mitigation plan applies, updates the desk's compliance guidance or training, and closes the file.

control.basis: MSA Compliance Process section 6.4.2: completed mitigation plan form within five business days of completion

next.condition: matter closed with an MSA disposition

evidence.note: Mitigation plan completion rule from the process; completion time estimated.

steps.name: Review the MSA inquiry or AESO referral
steps.description: The officer reads the MSA's letter or the AESO's referral notice, identifies the conduct, period and records requested and the response deadline, and plans who must provide what.

evidence.note: After a referral the MSA has sole carriage and may request information (section 5.2).

steps.name: Collect records for the response
steps.description: The officer extracts offers, restatements, dispatches, outage records, emails and chat for the period from the ETS, the ETRM and archives, and checks them for completeness before legal review.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Desk lead provides context for the events
steps.description: The real-time desk lead explains the offer strategy or operating decisions in the period, such as the reasons recorded for restatements or outages, and identifies the traders and operators involved.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Legal counsel reviews the inquiry response
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the record set and desk statement for privilege and exposure, advises on positions such as whether an offer reason was acceptable, and sets the line the response will take.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Draft the written response
steps.description: The officer drafts the written response or additional submission with the facts, records and mitigating circumstances, aiming to file within two weeks of a referral unless the MSA agrees an extension.

control.basis: MSA Compliance Process section 3.3: additional submissions within two weeks of a referral

exceptions.name: AESO referral
exceptions.description: The AESO's monitoring finds a suspected contravention first and refers it to the MSA; the company loses the self-report discount and a penalty is far more likely (77 percent of referred ISO rules matters in 2021).

exceptions.name: MSA follow-up questions
exceptions.description: The MSA asks for more data or explanation before deciding.

exceptions.name: Specified penalty
exceptions.description: The MSA issues a notice of specified penalty, which the company pays.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from logging the item to closure
benchmarks.population: Market rule compliance reviews and MSA matters of an Alberta generator

evidence.note: Derived: internal no-contravention reviews close within one to two weeks; matters filed with the MSA wait about 44 days on average (56 unresolved against 462 addressed a year), plus two to four weeks of internal preparation and close-out.

benchmarks.unit: share of ISO rules matters addressed in 2021

pain_points.description: Deciding whether a restatement reason or a delivery shortfall breaks the rule needs experience with the rule wording and past MSA decisions, and only a few officers have it.

evidence.note: Most matters concern restatements and dispatch delivery, where facts are routine but judgment calls are frequent.

pain_points.description: Fact gathering spans the ETS, historian, desk logs and chat, and must finish quickly to self-report within 30 days.

evidence.note: 30-day criterion from the forbearance criteria; effort estimated.

pain_points.description: Matters wait weeks to months at the MSA, so corrective actions and repeat-contravention counts must be tracked across many open files.

evidence.note: 56 ISO rules matters unresolved at the end of 2021.

assumptions: Self-identified issues from offer and restatement monitoring are modelled as case triggers; the organisation file lists offer records only as standing inputs.
MSA inquiries include AESO referrals, because after a referral the MSA has sole carriage of the matter and contacts the company.
The penalty payment request is routed to accounts payable (fin-pay-suppliers); the organisation file has no such link.
The MSA Compliance Process of December 2020 governed the reference period; it was later revoked and replaced, which does not change this 2019-2022 description.
No physical resources, travel or field wait causes apply to this office process.

sources.title: MSA Compliance Review 2021
sources.supports: 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 (437 in 2020), 91 percent self-reported; outcomes 341 forbearance, 75 notices of specified penalty, 44 no contravention; 56 matters unresolved at end of 2021; 10 percent of self-reported and 77 percent of AESO-referred matters received a specified penalty; most matters under sections 203.3 (restatements), 203.4, 201.7, 205.5 and 205.6; TransAlta Generation Partnership 8 penalty matters (19,500 CAD), TA Alberta Hydro LP 5 (8,000 CAD), TransAlta Corporation 1 (500 CAD) and TransAlta Generation Partnership 1 O&P ARS matter (2,250 CAD); 80 O&P ARS and 294 CIP ARS matters addressed; O&P ARS counts vary with the three-year audit cycle; no penalty disputed.

sources.title: MSA Compliance Process: ISO Rules and Reliability Standards (effective December 4, 2020, since revoked)
sources.supports: Self-report forms sent to compliance@albertamsa.ca copying the AESO; AESO referrals give the MSA sole carriage; additional submissions within two weeks of a referral; dispositions of forbearance, no contravention or notice of specified penalty under AUC Rules 019 and 027; forbearance criteria including a self-report within 30 days of the contravention and a compliance program with corrective actions; mitigation plans for reliability standards with completion reported within five business days; unpaid or disputed penalties go to the AUC.
